title: Dominant lifting through absolute normalization

source.place: Tag 035Q, part (4), normal-domain specialization of the universal property

proof.text: Dominance sends the generic point of Y to that of Z, by taking the image of its closure and using denseRange.closure_range. Stalk-map naturality gives m:Spec K(Y) -> Spec K(Z) with m;jZ=jY;g.

Apply Scheme.isIso_fromNormalization_restrict at the top open to normal integral Y, then remove top-open inclusions. Its already proved general Lean interface has no finite-type hypothesis, unlike the restricted blueprint wording.

Let a=m followed by Spec K(Z) -> Z.normalization. Lift (a,jY) to the pullback of the integral map Z.fromNormalization along g. Apply jY.normalizationDesc to the integral pullback projection, and precompose with the inverse of Y.fromNormalization. The first projection defines f:Y -> Z.normalization. The normalizationDesc equations give f;Z.fromNormalization=g and jY;f=a.
Every map between spectra of fields is dominant because the target has one point and the source is nonempty. Thus m and a are dominant, and jY;f=a implies f is dominant.

For dominant lifts f and f-prime, factor their generic restrictions through the generic point of Z.normalization. The generic-field isomorphism identifies that point with Spec K(Z). Postcomposition into Z gives equal maps. Cancel the monomorphism Spec K(Z) -> Z to deduce equality of the generic restrictions.

Z.fromNormalization is integral, hence affine and separated. The dominant jY is scheme-theoretically dominant because Y is reduced. Apply the relative separated-target rigidity theorem to the two lifts with equal generic restrictions.

lean.statement: theorem existsUnique_lift_normalization_of_dominant {Y Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y] [IsIntegral Z] (hY : ∀ y : Y, IsIntegrallyClosed (Y.presheaf.stalk y)) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [IsDominant g] : ∃! f : Y ⟶ Z.normalization, f ≫ Z.fromNormalization = g ∧ IsDominant f
